financials.source: Bellin Memorial Hospital Inc (EIN 39-0884478) IRS Form 990, FY ending September 2024, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. Total assets and liabilities are approximate from aggregated database reports; exact 990 Part X values not independently verified to the dollar.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Investment income of $14,303,977 reported on FY2024 990 (1.7% of revenue). Total assets $1,148,095,932, net assets $711,522,185 per ProPublica extract of FY2024 990. Part X balance sheet investment line items (lines 11-13: publicly traded securities, other securities, program-related investments) not independently verified — ProPublica, CauseIQ, Instrumentl, and GuideStar summaries do not break out securities balances. Bellin Health Foundation (EIN 39-1809171) held $6.3M in separate foundation investment assets as of September 2023. WHEFA bond continuing-disclosure filings on EMMA may contain audited financial statements with investment detail but were not accessed.
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Bellin Health Foundation (EIN 39-1809171) reported $6,335,656 in total investment assets as of September 30, 2023, comprising cash equivalents, fixed income, mutual funds, equities, and alternative investments. The hospital operating entity's investment portfolio is separate and substantially larger but the Part X total was not independently verified. Bellin merged with Gundersen Health System in December 2022; the combined entity rebranded as Emplify Health in April 2024 and operates 11 hospitals with ~15,000 employees across Wisconsin, Iowa, Minnesota, and Michigan.

bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: $130,000,000 — federal and Wisconsin tax-exempt fixed-rate bonds issued December 14, 2022, to finance Phase I of a five-story, 256,000 sq ft ambulatory surgery center and multi-specialty clinic in Ashwaubenon, WI, and a nursing unit expansion at Bellin Memorial Hospital in Green Bay

executiveComp.source: Bellin Memorial Hospital Inc (EIN 39-0884478) IRS Form 990 Schedule J, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer and Instrumentl 990 report. Woleske listed as Board Member/Executive Vice President with $1,775,439 reportable compensation and $238,231 other compensation. Woleske announced retirement effective July 1, 2025, after 26 years with Bellin Health.

communityBenefit.source: Bellin Health 2022 Community Benefits Report (FY ending September 2022) — $55,491,950 reported in subsidized health services. Wisconsin Hospital Association reports statewide community benefits of $2.3B in FY2023 and $2.2B in FY2024. Bellin-specific charity care breakout from Schedule H not independently verified for FY2024.

taxAdvantage.notes: Bellin Memorial Hospital's $130M in tax-exempt bonds (2022) provide interest cost savings vs. taxable financing. 340B participation as Rural Referral Center (340B ID: RRC520049-07) was terminated April 1, 2025 due to DSH percentage falling below statutory minimum. Bellin Health Oconto Hospital and related facilities remain registered as Critical Access Hospitals in the 340B program.

accusation: Bellin Health, operating within the Emplify Health system with over $1.1 billion in total assets and $711 million in net assets, collected $130 million in tax-exempt bond financing and over $2 million in annual CEO compensation while its 340B drug discount participation was terminated for failing to meet disproportionate-share thresholds, raising questions about whether its tax-exempt wealth is flowing to the communities it claims to serve.
